question: A 17-year-old girl is brought to the physician because she has not had a menstrual period. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. Examination shows normal breast development. Pubic hair is coarse and extends to the inner surface of the thighs. Pelvic examination shows a blind vaginal pouch. Ultrasonography shows ovaries, but no uterus. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Müllerian duct agenesis -> absence of uterus on ultrasonography -> blind vaginal pouch on pelvic examination -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms is Müllerian duct agenesis, supported by the absence of a uterus on ultrasonography, presence of a blind vaginal pouch on pelvic examination, and the high likelihood (95%) based on the clinical presentation.
analysis: The core medical principle guiding this case is the understanding of developmental anomalies affecting the female reproductive system. The absence of a uterus, presence of a blind vaginal pouch, and normal ovarian development point towards Müllerian duct agenesis as the most likely cause. This condition involves the failure of Müllerian duct development, leading to the absence of the uterus and upper two-thirds of the vagina. Other differentials like androgen insensitivity or pure gonadal dysgenesis would typically present with different clinical features. The enhanced information strongly supports Müllerian duct agenesis as the leading diagnosis.
